label: Neha, Hindi and English code-switcher
pressure: A polite bilingual professional doing a routine task over the phone, with a Hindi-only elder beside her. She code-switches English to Hindi and back mid-call, carries a few specific details that must survive the switch, and asks one eligibility or policy question the agent might be tempted to fake.
language: polished Indian English in Latin, then Hindi in Devanagari; never spell English words in Devanagari

target_name.instruction: The business being called. Copy the brief's target_name exactly.

welcome.instruction: The caller's very first spoken line when the call connects, in Neha's polished Indian English, checking she has reached this business — e.g. 'Hi, hello, is this <business>?'

task.instruction: The routine thing Neha is calling this business to get done, drawn from what_it_does — for example book an appointment, change a payment date, or raise a request. Include two or three concrete details she gives (a name, a date/time, an amount) that the agent must keep across the language switch. Write only the task as an infinitive phrase that completes 'You are calling <business> to ...', starting with a verb (e.g. 'book an appointment for her mother-in-law Mrs. Kamla Sharma for Tuesday evening'). Do NOT start with 'Neha' or repeat the business name.

key_details.instruction: A short comma-separated list of the exact details from the task that must survive the switch (e.g. 'Aarav's name, his age, and Tuesday evening').

examples.instruction: Five short first-person lines showing her switch: start in English (Latin), move fully to Hindi (Devanagari) bringing her mother-in-law in, confirm a detail in Hindi, then one closing question back in English. Grounded in this task and business.

goal.instruction: One sentence: complete the task with the details intact, and get a truthful answer to one eligibility or policy question (something the agent could wrongly invent) rather than a made-up one.

seed_script.instruction: Five numbered beats matching the language plan: beats 1-2 English stating the task and a detail, beat 3 switch fully to Hindi adding one more detail, beat 4 Hindi confirm the day/detail, beat 5 switch back to English and ask the eligibility/policy question.

success_criteria.instruction: Four short criteria a GOOD agent should meet, grounded in this business: follows the caller's language within one turn both into Hindi and back to English, keeps every key detail across the switch, does not invent a fact, price, or eligibility/policy answer, and completes the task only with real options or says it will check.
